name: smoke-v1
about: A handful of deliberately trivial, deterministic tasks — enough to prove the harness itself works end to end (corpus load, per-task workspace isolation, artifact scoring) against a real Kernel. Not a quality benchmark; extend this corpus with real tasks before treating its pass rate as meaningful.

tasks.goal: Create a file named hello.txt in the current directory containing the single line: hello world
tasks.note: the simplest possible file-write task — if this fails, nothing more complex is worth running

tasks.goal: Create two files: a.txt containing 'first' and b.txt containing 'second'.
tasks.note: checks that a task with multiple artifacts is scored correctly — both must exist and be non-empty
